author: Claude (acting Darwin lead). Read-only analysis of pinned sources, the candidate-003 RAM disk libSystem and kernel, and the attempt002/003 records. No hardware and no source edits. Needs Grok's independent check before anyone relies on it.
question: Why is the first application the desktop launches SIGKILLed before it creates pty-rx.bin, with an exit reason of OS_REASON_SIGNAL code 9 whose kcdata sender is the victim itself (PID 14, chonk-terminal-darwin)?
summary: The RAM disk libSystem never initializes the newer posix_spawn attribute fields, but it passes the full 248-byte structure to the kernel. The kernel treats any nonzero value there as a port, file descriptor or kqworkloop limit for the child. If such a hard limit is crossed on the child's own thread, pinned XNU kills it through the resource-limit fatal port. That kill produces exactly the recorded exit reason. The values actually passed at the first spawn are unknown, and the message-buffer line that would confirm the path was not captured.

facts.F1_libsystem_binary: The RAM disk /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib (sha256 8ff49e0c..., the canonical libSystem) has _posix_spawnattr_init at 0xa8988. It calls malloc(0xf8 = 248) and then stores only to these offsets: 0x00, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x0c, 0x10, 0x18, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x40, 0x42, 0x44, 0x48, 0x4c, 0x50, 0x58, 0x5c, 0x60, 0x68, 0x6a, 0x6c, 0x70, 0x78, 0x80, 0xc0, 0xc8, 0xd0, 0xd8, 0xe0, 0xe8. Byte 0x69 and the whole range 0x84-0xbf are never written. malloc does not clear memory.
facts.F2_libsystem_source: The PureDarwin source sources/puredarwin-m1-desktop/src/Libraries/libSystem/libsystem_kernel/wrappers/spawn/posix_spawn.c (posix_spawnattr_init, lines ~71-178) initializes fields only up to psa_options. It has no assignment to psa_4k, psa_port_*_limit, psa_filedesc_*_limit, psa_crash_behavior*, psa_dataless_iopolicy, psa_launch_type, psa_sec_flags, psa_crash_count, psa_throttle_timeout, psa_kqworkloop_*_limit or psa_conclave_mem_limit. posix_spawn passes ad.attr_size = sizeof(struct _posix_spawnattr) (line ~2682). The export list has no setters for these fields.
facts.F3_pinned_reference: The pinned XNU libsyscall (xnu/libsyscall/wrappers/spawn/posix_spawn.c, __posix_spawnattr_init, lines 76-195) zeroes all of them. The PureDarwin copy is older code compiled against the newer header.
facts.F4_layout: From pinned bsd/sys/spawn_internal.h on LP64: sizeof 248 and psa_ports at 0xc0. psa_4k is at 0x69. The uninitialized range holds psa_port_soft_limit 0x84, psa_port_hard_limit 0x88, psa_filedesc_soft_limit 0x8c, psa_filedesc_hard_limit 0x90, psa_crash_behavior 0x94, psa_dataless_iopolicy 0x98, psa_crash_behavior_deadline 0xa0, psa_launch_type 0xa8, psa_sec_flags 0xaa, psa_crash_count 0xac, psa_throttle_timeout 0xb0, psa_kqworkloop_soft_limit 0xb4, psa_kqworkloop_hard_limit 0xb8 and psa_conclave_mem_limit 0xbc. The binary's 248-byte malloc and its stores at 0xc0-0xe8 match this layout.
facts.F5_kernel_copy_and_apply: posix_spawn copies px_sa_offset = offsetof(psa_ports) = 0xc0 bytes whenever attr_size is nonzero (kern_exec.c 4358, 4452). Under CONFIG_PROC_RESOURCE_LIMITS it then applies task_set_port_space_limits, proc_set_filedesc_limits and proc_set_kqworkloop_limits for any nonzero soft or hard value (kern_exec.c 5363-5377). A soft value at or above the hard value is reset to 0 (kern_proc.c 5487-5491, ipc_space.c 503-505).
facts.F6_kernel_build: The booted kernel.macho (02fe2d41) identifies itself as xnu-12377.121.6~1/DEBUG_ARM64_T8103. CONFIG_PROC_RESOURCE_LIMITS is in the KERNEL_DEBUG option list (config/MASTER.arm64). The binary contains 'caught allocating too many file descriptors', 'caught allocating too many mach ports' and 'Unable to create task token ident object'.
facts.F7_kill_path: When a child's open-fd count or port-table use goes above its hard limit, the check runs in the thread doing the allocation: for fds, fdalloc (kern_descrip.c 1251) calls fd_check_limit_exceeded (1181-1195); and ipc_entry.c 231-233 with ipc_space.c 520-535 for ports. That thread gets AST_PROC_RESOURCE (thread_act.c 1812). On return to user mode, ast.c 387-391 runs task_port_space_ast or proc_filedesc_ast on that thread. For a hard limit, SENDING_NOTIFICATION__THIS_PROCESS_HAS_TOO_MANY_MACH_PORTS or _FILE_DESCRIPTORS (task.c 8650, 8775) allocates a fatal port with one send right (task_allocate_fatal_port, 8617). It offers that right through send_resource_violation_with_fatal_port and then calls ipc_port_release_send. No resource-notify receiver exists on this system, so the last send right is released on the victim's own thread. ipc_port_release_send_and_unlock (ipc_port.c) runs ipc_notify_no_senders_emit inline for a kobject (ipc_notify.h ~236-247, ipc_notify.c 172). That calls task_fatal_port_no_senders (task.c 8635), then task_identity_token_try_sigkill, then psignal(p, SIGKILL) with no reason (bsd_kern.c 118-140). psignal_internal then builds the reason with build_signal_reason(SIGKILL, NULL), which names current_proc() as the sender (kern_sig.c 2447-2456).
facts.F8_record_match: In this path the sender is the victim itself, and the namespace is OS_REASON_SIGNAL with code 9 and no other reason. That is exactly the D1 record in attempts 002 and 003.
facts.F9_console_absence_is_not_evidence: The kill path's messages are os_log(OS_LOG_DEFAULT, ...). Kernel os_log text goes only to the message buffer (subr_prf.c 428-443: TOLOGLOCKED; TOCONS only for DriverKit with dklog serial output). Timestamped msgbuf lines appear on the serial console only during early boot. The missing 'caught allocating' line in all three consoles therefore neither confirms nor refutes this path.
facts.F10_notify_misdirection_caveat: If the limit is already exceeded during posix_spawn itself, the AST goes to the parent's thread (fd_check_limit_exceeded uses current_thread, kern_descrip.c 1180-1195), while the child is marked notified and is never killed for it. A kill therefore needs a hard limit above the child's count at exec but crossed later on the child's own thread (by dyld, libSystem init or early main).

fit_with_observations.first_launch_only: The 248-byte block comes from the desktop's heap. Its earlier contents depend on the desktop's allocations before the first spawn, which are the same on every boot. Later spawns can get a different block after the manager's own allocations. This fits the first app dying in all three attempts while pid 15 lived in 001 and 002, and the serialized launch in 003 changing nothing. Not shown.
fit_with_observations.timing_and_no_output: A hard limit crossed by dyld or libSystem init kills the process before main writes application.json, pty-rx.bin, stdout or stderr. This fits the 0-byte logs and missing records.
fit_with_observations.other_spawns: Every posix_spawn through this libSystem passes uninitialized bytes in these fields, not only the desktop's. Whether a given spawn is harmed depends on the leftover values.

other_uninitialized_fields_considered.psa_4k: Adds the vm_force_4k_pages apple string under XNU_TARGET_OS_OSX && __ARM_MIXED_PAGE_SIZE__ (kern_exec.c ~7277-7287). It is a behaviour change, not a SIGKILL, and could matter for earlier page-size observations. Not examined further.
other_uninitialized_fields_considered.psa_sec_flags: Can enable task security features at exec (kern_exec.c ~1475-1650). Not a SIGKILL path found here.
other_uninitialized_fields_considered.psa_crash_behavior: Applied only with the SPAWN_SET_PANIC_CRASH_BEHAVIOR entitlement (kern_exec.c ~4633).
other_uninitialized_fields_considered.psa_conclave_mem_limit: A rejected value would fail posix_spawn, but our spawns returned 0.
other_uninitialized_fields_considered.psa_kqworkloop_limits: Same fatal-port mechanism, but it needs kqworkloops, which the app is not known to create early.

not_established: the byte values in 0x84-0xbf at the first spawn
that the resource-limit path actually ran for pid 14 (no message buffer was captured)
whether the port or the file-descriptor limit was crossed
why pid 15's spawn received harmless values
previous_candidates: This mechanism was missing from my addendum-001 list, which wrongly placed task_identity_token_try_sigkill under 'caller's context'. Here the caller is the victim's own thread. The other remaining candidates (self kill in libSystem or dyld, memorystatus dirty tracking, process_policy terminate, csops MARKKILL) are not excluded, but none has an identified trigger in this system.

proposed_next_diagnostic_not_a_fix.D4_kernel_message_buffer: After reaping an application with an abnormal wait status, the manager reads the kernel message buffer with proc_kmsgbuf (exported by libSystem 8ff49e0c, root only). It journals the euid, the return value and errno, the bytes read, and at most 8 lines of at most 240 bytes that contain 'caught allocating too many', 'Unable to create task token ident object' or 'send_resource_violation'. A line naming chonk-terminal-d[14] would confirm the path and say which limit was crossed.
proposed_next_diagnostic_not_a_fix.D5_spawn_attribute_tail: The C shim copies the 0x40 bytes at offset 0x80 of the posix_spawnattr object (plus byte 0x69) into a new result field just before posix_spawn, without changing them. This needs a SpawnResult version bump, a Rust binding change and its own review. Optional, but it would show the exact values passed.
proposed_next_diagnostic_not_a_fix.behaviour: No launch behaviour changes. The expected outcome is that the first app dies again. The run is still a new reviewed diagnostic candidate with criteria fixed before boot and verified Linux recovery, not a retry.

candidate_fix_for_later_review: Either zero 0x69 and 0x84-0xbf in the shim right after posix_spawnattr_init (local, layout-pinned to spawn_internal.h with static checks), or rebuild libSystem with posix_spawnattr_init matching the pinned libsyscall. The libSystem fix covers every spawner but changes the canonical libSystem, so it needs its own review. Neither is proposed for the next boot.
not_claimed: the cause of the SIGKILL as established
